e.etymology: A pet form of Oswald or Oscar, with the -ie ending. It is now given on its own to boys and, more recently, girls.
namesakes: Ozzie Smith (Hall of Fame Cardinals shortstop)
Ozzie Nelson (star of The Adventures of Ozzie and Harriet)

assoc.t: rock singer Ozzy Osbourne, who spelled it Ozzy
sounds like Aussie, slang for an Australian

e.etymology: The name of a revered sage of the Vedas, also honored in Tamil tradition, and the Indian name for the bright star Canopus. A traditional reading of the Sanskrit is mover of mountains.
A respelling of Elaina, a form of Elaine, the Old French version of Helen. Greek Helene is usually explained as torch or shining light.
The feminine of Silvius, from Latin silva, forest. In Roman legend Rhea Silvia was the mother of Romulus and Remus, and a 6th-century Saint Silvia was the mother of Pope Gregory the Great.
namesakes: Queen Silvia of Sweden (queen consort since 1976)

e.etymology: An African American coinage of the later 20th century, built on the Ja- beginning and the -von ending of names like Devon and Davon.
From Arabic sami, high or exalted. The same spelling is a Finnish form of Samuel and an English short form of Samuel or Samantha.
namesakes: Sami Zayn (WWE wrestler)

assoc.t: the Sami, indigenous people of northern Scandinavia

e.etymology: From Hebrew gad, fortune, and el, God. A Gaddiel is one of the twelve scouts Moses sends into Canaan, and later Jewish mysticism names an angel Gadiel. Today it is most used by Spanish speakers.
A less common spelling of Liliana, a Latin-styled elaboration of Lilian that goes back to Latin lilium, lily.
From the Welsh surname, a form of the name Gwyn, white, fair or blessed. Wynn is also the name of an Old English letter, from the word for joy.
namesakes: Steve Wynn (Las Vegas casino developer)

assoc.t: Wynn, the Las Vegas casino resort company

e.note: Sounds exactly like the word win.

e.etymology: From Arabic safa, purity or clearness. Safa is also one of the two hills in Mecca, Safa and Marwa, between which pilgrims walk during the Hajj.

assoc.t: Safa, a hill in Mecca visited on the Hajj

e.etymology: A respelling of Creed, the English word for a statement of belief, from Latin credo, I believe.

assoc.t: Apollo and Adonis Creed of the Rocky and Creed films
Creed, the rock band behind Higher

e.etymology: In Igbo, Mazi is a title of respect for a man, much like Mister. How the American given name arose is not documented.
From the plant, a low shrub with purple and pink flowers that covers the moors of Scotland and northern England. It is one of the plant names taken up for girls in the 19th century.
namesakes: Heather Locklear (actress in Dynasty and Melrose Place)
Heather Graham (actress in Boogie Nights)

assoc.t: the clique of Heathers in the 1988 film Heathers
a Heather, slang for an enviably popular girl

e.note: Most American Heathers were born in the 1970s and 80s, so the name can read as a mom name today.

e.etymology: From the gemstone, whose name goes back to Greek adamas, unbreakable. It came into use as a given name in the US in the 1980s.
namesakes: Neil Diamond (singer of Sweet Caroline)

e.etymology: The feminine form of Eric, from Old Norse Eiríkr, usually read as ever or sole ruler. Erica is also the Latin name of the heath plant, which helped the name along.
namesakes: Erica Kane (Susan Lucci's character on All My Children)
Erica Jong (author of Fear of Flying)

assoc.t: Erica, Bank of America's virtual assistant

e.etymology: From Sanskrit isha, lord or ruler; the feminine form is a name of the goddess Durga. Isha is also the Arabic name of the Muslim night prayer.
The French feminine of Adrien, from the Latin name Hadrianus, a man from Hadria, a town in northern Italy that also gave its name to the Adriatic Sea.
namesakes: Adrienne Rich (poet)
Adrienne Barbeau (actress in Maude and Escape from New York)
Adrienne Bailon (singer and talk show host)

e.etymology: An Italian men's name, a form of Carmelo shaped by Spanish Carmen. Both honor Our Lady of Mount Carmel, whose name is Hebrew for garden or orchard.
namesakes: Carmine Falcone (Gotham crime boss in the Batman stories)

assoc.t: carmine, a deep red color and pigment

e.etymology: A form of Jasmine that follows the Arabic and Persian name Yasmin, from the Persian word for the jasmine flower.
namesakes: Yasmine Bleeth (Baywatch actress)

e.etymology: A trimmed spelling of Emery or Emory, an English surname from the Norman name Aimeri, built on Germanic elements for vigor and ruler.
The French form of Peter, from Greek petros, stone or rock, the name Jesus gave the apostle Simon. Pierre is still the everyday French word for stone.
namesakes: Pierre Cardin (fashion designer)
Pierre-Auguste Renoir (Impressionist painter)
Pierre Trudeau (prime minister of Canada)

assoc.t: Pierre, capital of South Dakota (said like peer)

e.note: In the US the name reads as unmistakably French and is a stock name for a Frenchman in jokes.

e.etymology: A modern American coinage in the family of Kalia, Kaliyah and Aaliyah, with no meaning of its own.
A respelling of Liam, the Irish short form of Uilliam (William), from Germanic elements meaning will and helmet. The y spelling is especially popular in France.
A respelling of Eliana, in Hebrew eli, my God, and ana, he answered. The -yanah ending follows the style of Aaliyah.
A surname built on Jacob, from Latin Jacobi, of Jacob. Jacob comes from Hebrew Yaakov, traditionally read as holder of the heel or supplanter.
namesakes: Jacoby Ellsbury (Red Sox and Yankees outfielder)
Jacoby Brissett (NFL quarterback)
Jacoby Jones (Ravens receiver, Super Bowl XLVII star)

e.etymology: The French and Czech form of Lucy, from Latin Lucia, the feminine of the Roman first name Lucius, from lux, light. Saint Lucia of Syracuse made it a favorite across Europe.
namesakes: Lucie Arnaz (actress, daughter of Lucille Ball and Desi Arnaz)

e.etymology: Probably a respelling of Malia, the Hawaiian form of Mary. The -ah ending follows names like Aaliyah and Mariah.
A respelling of Emery, an English and French surname from the Norman name Aimeri, built on Germanic elements for vigor and ruler.
A Xhosa and Zulu name from South Africa, built on the verb xola, to be at peace or to forgive. There it is a men's name, while American parents give it mostly to girls.
e.note: In Xhosa and Zulu the X is a click sound and the name is a man's; Americans say zoh-LAH-nee.

e.etymology: The modern Hebrew form of Ethan, from eitan, firm, strong or long-lasting. In the Bible Ethan the Ezrahite is a wise man credited with Psalm 89.
A modern American blend of Mae and the -lyn ending, in the pattern of Raelyn and Kaelyn.
For girls, a 20th-century name from Welsh tegan, pet or darling, from teg, fair. It is also a spelling of Teagan, from an Irish surname built on Tadhg, poet.
namesakes: Tegan Quin (half of the indie pop duo Tegan and Sara)

assoc.t: Tegan and Sara, the Canadian indie pop duo
